sections.title: Grade 7 skills
sections.description: The most important words, reading, grammar and writing from Grade 7.

sections.title: Grade 6 skills
sections.description: Key words, reading, grammar and writing from Grade 6.

questions.question: Which word describes a person who is kind and generous, and wants to help others?
questions.options: benevolent | vulnerable | belligerent | vindictive
questions.correctAnswer: benevolent
questions.explanation: A benevolent person is kind-hearted and generous — like a neighbour who shares food at a festival.

questions.question: A steward who stands quietly by the gate, watching carefully and staying alert for any trouble, is ___.
questions.options: vigilant | frivolous | complacent | naive
questions.correctAnswer: vigilant
questions.explanation: Vigilant means watchful and alert, always ready to notice a problem before it grows.

questions.question: Choose the word that means 'to work together with others towards one shared goal'.
questions.options: demonstrate | collaborate | infuriate | retaliate
questions.correctAnswer: collaborate
questions.explanation: When people collaborate, they join their efforts — like classmates planting trees together.

questions.question: Every year the water level in the river gets smaller and smaller. Which word describes this?
questions.options: dwindles | flourishes | augments | convenes
questions.correctAnswer: dwindles
questions.explanation: Dwindle means to gradually become smaller or less, like a river shrinking over time.

questions.question: Which word names a person who helps different groups communicate and work together?
questions.options: opposition | liaison | delegate | amendment
questions.correctAnswer: liaison
questions.explanation: A liaison passes messages between groups so that everyone stays informed.

questions.question: Which compound adjective is written correctly before the noun it describes?
questions.options: a gold embroidered robe | a gold-embroidered robe | a goldembroidered robe | a gold embroidered-robe
questions.correctAnswer: a gold-embroidered robe
questions.explanation: Compound adjectives that come before a noun join their two words with a hyphen: gold-embroidered.

questions.question: Two hundred seedlings ___ every month by the eco-club.
questions.options: is planted | are planted | are planting | is planting
questions.correctAnswer: are planted
questions.explanation: The present passive is formed with are + past participle, and seedlings is plural, so it takes are planted.

questions.question: Endangered species ___ by law.
questions.options: must protect | must be protect | must be protected | must protecting
questions.correctAnswer: must be protected
questions.explanation: A modal passive needs modal + be + past participle: must be protected.

questions.question: Rohan said, 'I do not believe this video is real.' Which sentence reports his words correctly?
questions.options: Rohan said that he does not believe the video is real. | Rohan said that he did not believe the video was real. | Rohan said that I did not believe this video was real. | Rohan said he not believe the video was real.
questions.correctAnswer: Rohan said that he did not believe the video was real.
questions.explanation: In reported speech the tense steps back one, and I becomes he: did not believe, was real.

questions.question: ___ the headline nor the article gave the reporter's real name.
questions.options: Both | Either | Neither | Every
questions.correctAnswer: Neither
questions.explanation: Neither pairs with nor and rejects both options — here, neither the headline nor the article named the reporter.

questions.question: A passage says: 'Watch how people behave at any festival and you will notice the same qualities appearing again and again. The diligent organisers arrive first and leave last.' What does this suggest about festivals?
questions.options: Festivals only reward people who arrive early. | Festivals show the values a community wants children to learn. | Festivals are mainly about the food that is served. | Festivals happen only once a year.
questions.correctAnswer: Festivals show the values a community wants children to learn.
questions.explanation: The passage calls festivals a performance of the values a community wants its children to inherit.

questions.question: A passage compares festivals in Ethiopia, Lamu, Iran, Somalia and the United States, then concludes: 'The customs differ from country to country, but the pattern is remarkably similar.' According to the passage, what do these festivals have in common?
questions.options: They are all held in November. | They all involve fire, food and storytelling. | They all celebrate the same historical event. | They all last exactly thirteen days.
questions.correctAnswer: They all involve fire, food and storytelling.
questions.explanation: The passage names fire, food and storytelling as universal ways festivals draw people together.

questions.question: Around the campfire, Amal says that a forest is not saved in a day, but it can be lost in one. What is Amal's warning?
questions.options: Forests take a long time to protect but can be destroyed quickly. | Forests can never be saved. | Campfires are dangerous for forests. | Forests grow back overnight.
questions.correctAnswer: Forests take a long time to protect but can be destroyed quickly.
questions.explanation: Amal is contrasting slow, careful protection with sudden, fast destruction.

questions.question: A conservation fact sheet ends: 'Conservation is sustained by significant small actions, so every visitor must endeavour to leave no trace.' What does this fact suggest matters most for conservation?
questions.options: Only large organisations can protect forests. | Small, careful actions by everyone add up to real conservation. | Visitors should avoid forests completely. | Conservation happens automatically over time.
questions.correctAnswer: Small, careful actions by everyone add up to real conservation.
questions.explanation: The sentence links conservation directly to many small, significant actions, not just big projects.

questions.question: A headline reads: 'BREAKING: A source close to the Ministry confirmed the plan.' Why is naming the source this way a warning sign?
questions.options: It uses the word BREAKING. | No name or title is given, so nobody can check the claim. | It mentions the Ministry. | It is written using capital letters.
questions.correctAnswer: No name or title is given, so nobody can check the claim.
questions.explanation: An unnamed source cannot be checked or held responsible if the claim turns out to be false.

questions.question: Which opening line would most effectively grab an audience's attention at the start of a persuasive speech about protecting forests?
questions.options: Forests are found in many countries. | Do we really want to live in a world without forests? | This speech is about trees. | Trees are green and tall.
questions.correctAnswer: Do we really want to live in a world without forests?
questions.explanation: A rhetorical question draws the audience in and makes them consider the issue immediately, unlike a flat statement of fact.

questions.question: A good lead paragraph in a news article should answer which of these?
questions.options: Only the writer's opinion | The five Ws: who, what, when, where and why | A list of every vocabulary word in the unit | The reader's own opinion
questions.correctAnswer: The five Ws: who, what, when, where and why
questions.explanation: Journalists open with the five Ws so readers get the key facts straight away.

questions.question: Why should a writer name a clear source, such as 'the Ministry's website', rather than writing 'a source close to the Ministry'?
questions.options: Named sources take up more space on the page. | A named source can be checked, so the claim is more trustworthy. | Named sources are always more exciting to read. | It makes the article longer.
questions.correctAnswer: A named source can be checked, so the claim is more trustworthy.
questions.explanation: Responsible writers attribute claims to sources a reader could actually verify.

questions.question: In a balanced discussion essay, which phrase best signals that the writer is about to consider the opposite viewpoint?
questions.options: In conclusion | On the other hand | For example | Firstly
questions.correctAnswer: On the other hand
questions.explanation: 'On the other hand' is the standard signal for turning to a contrasting or opposing point in balanced writing.

questions.question: A trip guide written for younger students beginning their first hike should mainly use language that is ___.
questions.options: highly technical and full of scientific terms | clear, encouraging and easy for a younger reader to follow | written only in the past tense | copied directly from a dictionary
questions.correctAnswer: clear, encouraging and easy for a younger reader to follow
questions.explanation: Good writers match their language to their audience — younger readers need clear, encouraging instructions.

questions.question: The mountain path looked safe but was full of loose rocks. Which word describes the path?
questions.options: meagre | classical | treacherous | humble
questions.correctAnswer: treacherous
questions.explanation: Treacherous means dangerous even though it seems safe — just like that path.

questions.question: During the match, the radio ___ described every goal as it happened.
questions.options: commentary | conduction | caravan | script
questions.correctAnswer: commentary
questions.explanation: A commentary is a spoken description of an event, given while it happens.

questions.question: To completely change the form of something so that it becomes something new is to ___ it.
questions.options: transform | relocate | analyse | preserve
questions.correctAnswer: transform
questions.explanation: Transform means to change something's form so completely that it becomes something new.

questions.question: After weeks of watering, the dusty valley finally turned green and the plants grew strongly. We can say the plants began to ___.
questions.options: flourish | collide | disgrace | overthrow
questions.correctAnswer: flourish
questions.explanation: Flourish means to grow well and thrive, as the plants did once the valley was watered.

questions.question: A vulture ___ the environment by eating dead animals.
questions.options: clean | cleans | cleaning | is clean
questions.correctAnswer: cleans
questions.explanation: For a singular subject like a vulture, the present simple adds -s: cleans.

questions.question: The cheetah is a predator ___ runs faster than any other land animal.
questions.options: who | which | that | where
questions.correctAnswer: that
questions.explanation: A defining relative clause about an animal uses that (or which), with no comma, to say exactly which predator.

questions.question: 'I need the test results,' said the doctor. Which sentence reports this correctly?
questions.options: The doctor said that she needs the test results. | The doctor said that she needed the test results. | The doctor said that I needed the test results. | The doctor say that she needed the test results.
questions.correctAnswer: The doctor said that she needed the test results.
questions.explanation: Reported speech shifts the tense back one step and changes the pronoun to match the speaker: needed, she.

questions.question: Which phrase puts the adjectives in the correct order?
questions.options: a wooden large rectangular board | a large rectangular wooden board | a rectangular wooden large board | a large wooden rectangular board
questions.correctAnswer: a large rectangular wooden board
questions.explanation: Adjectives follow a set order: size, then shape, then material — large, rectangular, wooden.

questions.question: A passage explains: 'These plants are called producers because they produce the energy that the entire chain depends on.' Why does the passage call plants 'producers'?
questions.options: They are the largest living things in an ecosystem. | They produce the energy that the whole food chain depends on. | They only grow in the rainy season. | They are eaten by every animal.
questions.correctAnswer: They produce the energy that the whole food chain depends on.
questions.explanation: The passage explains that plants are named producers because every other animal in the chain depends on the energy they make.

questions.question: A passage says: 'The balance of nature is treacherous — it can look strong, but it is easily broken.' What does this sentence suggest about ecosystems?
questions.options: Ecosystems always stay exactly the same. | Ecosystems can look stable but are easily damaged. | Ecosystems are dangerous to visit. | Ecosystems only exist in East Africa.
questions.correctAnswer: Ecosystems can look stable but are easily damaged.
questions.explanation: The sentence warns that an ecosystem's strength can be an illusion, since it is easily broken.

questions.question: A passage says: 'No profession stands alone; each one is a link in a chain that reaches across the whole town.' What is the main idea of this passage about professions?
questions.options: Only doctors and lawyers have important jobs. | Different jobs in a community depend on and support each other. | Everyone should have the same job. | People should work alone whenever possible.
questions.correctAnswer: Different jobs in a community depend on and support each other.
questions.explanation: The passage describes professions as links in one chain, each depending on the others.

questions.question: A passage about a mural project says: 'None of these projects began with money... [they needed] the willingness to keep going when the first attempt failed.' According to the passage, what made the project possible?
questions.options: A large grant from the government | Donated materials and the group's own effort and commitment | Expensive professional equipment | Paid artists hired from another city
questions.correctAnswer: Donated materials and the group's own effort and commitment
questions.explanation: The passage credits donated supplies and the volunteers' own determination, not money, for the project's success.

questions.question: Why does Tariq, a radio commentator, choose his words carefully when explaining the day's events?
questions.options: So that listeners can easily understand what he is saying | So that his broadcast lasts longer | So that only experts can understand him | So that he does not have to write a script
questions.correctAnswer: So that listeners can easily understand what he is saying
questions.explanation: A good speaker or writer chooses words with the audience in mind, so the message is clear to them.

questions.question: A well-organised research report about an animal should group information into ___.
questions.options: one long paragraph with everything mixed together | clear paragraphs, such as appearance, habitat, diet and threats | a single sentence per fact with no paragraphs at all | random order, so the reader stays guessing
questions.correctAnswer: clear paragraphs, such as appearance, habitat, diet and threats
questions.explanation: Organising facts into clear, labelled paragraphs helps the reader follow the information easily.

questions.question: Which sentence best summarises a passage's main message about professions in a community?
questions.options: Only people with university degrees have real jobs. | Every job matters, and people rely on each other to keep a community running. | Working alone is always better than working in a team. | Some professions are more important than others.
questions.correctAnswer: Every job matters, and people rely on each other to keep a community running.
questions.explanation: A good summary captures the passage's central point in one clear sentence, without extra detail.

questions.question: An art project description opens: 'I would like to explain my project, Wind Valley Walls.' How does this opening sentence mainly help the reader?
questions.options: It hides the topic until the very end. | It introduces the project clearly right at the start. | It lists every material that was used. | It avoids any mention of the writer's own project.
questions.correctAnswer: It introduces the project clearly right at the start.
questions.explanation: A clear opening tells the reader straight away what the piece of writing is about.
